value.title: Review round 1 — a worked example
value.model: a capable model, named so results can be compared across them
value.note: A review as rows rather than prose. The point is not tidiness: 'which findings were refuted, and on what grounds' is a question worth asking across reviews and across models, and prose cannot answer it. Every finding carries an address, so a reader goes to the code rather than to the reviewer's description of the code.

value.finding: Deep scan reports the first match and stops, so a shadowed duplicate in a later root is never reported — the precedence rule holds but its visibility half does not.
The generated module's header does not say how to regenerate it, so a reader who finds it first has no way back to the source.
Should the id-prefix registry be a schema declaration rather than a CLI constant?
value.note: Recorded as a question, not a defect: it is a design direction, and answering it inside a review round would be deciding it in the wrong room.
value.receipt: Jordan, 2026-08-04: "keep away from it — later iteration maybe, not now"

value.finding: Dim-0: precedence was inverted in the resolver on purpose. The planted-bad fixture FIRED, so the control measures the behaviour it claims to.
Dim-0: the baked module was edited away from its source on purpose. NOTHING failed — the suite compared the module to itself, so the drift check had only ever been run against good input.

value.rationale: Confirmed by reading the resolver and reproducing it against a two-root fixture. The scan now collects every match and reports the shadowed ones with their paths.
The header now names the generator and the regeneration command.
A real question with a real cost, but it changes an address surface. Recorded against the plan rather than answered here.
value.receipt: Jordan, 2026-08-04: "keep away from it — later iteration maybe, not now"

value.rationale: The control fired as claimed. Recorded so the NEXT review can see this control was already probed and probe a different one.

The reported mechanism was wrong — the suite does compare the module to its sources, and the mutation was applied to a stale copy in the reviewer's working tree. But the round-trip HAD only ever been proven one way, so a hermetic both-ways control was added anyway. A refuted finding that still improves the code is worth recording as refuted: the next reviewer should not re-open it on the same reasoning.
